html:
Rwanda under Belgian rule was the northern half of Ruanda-Urundi, the territory Belgium ran from 1916 until Rwanda became independent in 1962. The southern half became Burundi.

Both had been old kingdoms, taken into German East Africa in the 1890s. Belgian troops from the Congo seized them in World War I, and from 1922 Belgium held them under a League of Nations mandate.

Belgium ruled through the Tutsi king, the mwami, and a Tutsi chiefly class, and Catholic missions spread fast. In 1933 it issued identity cards that fixed every person as Hutu, Tutsi or Twa. Groups that had once been fluid became rigid, legal categories.

In 1959 a Hutu revolt drove out many Tutsi, and the monarchy fell. Rwanda became independent as a Hutu-led republic in 1962. The divisions hardened under Belgian rule led in the end to the genocide of 1994.
sum: Rwanda under Belgian rule was the northern half of Ruanda-Urundi, the territory Belgium ran from 1916 until Rwanda became independent in 1962. The southern half became Burundi.
